title: 2026 Mid-Year Business Review
subtitle: Performance Analysis & Strategic Outlook
author: Marcus Chen, VP Strategy
executive_summary: This mid-year review examines Meridian Capital Partners' performance across all business units for the first half of 2026. Revenue grew 31% year-over-year, driven by expansion into the Asia-Pacific corridor and strong performance in our private credit portfolio. AUM reached $4.2B, ahead of the full-year target of $3.9B. Key challenges include margin compression in the advisory segment and elevated operational costs from the London office build-out.

subsections.title: Revenue & AUM
subsections.content: Total revenue for H1 2026 reached $182.4M, up from $139.2M in H1 2025. Management fees contributed 64% of revenue at $116.7M. Assets under management grew to $4.2B as of June 30, surpassing our $3.9B full-year target six months early. The private credit fund was the standout performer, returning 14.2% net annualized.

subsections.title: Cost Structure
subsections.content: Operating expenses increased 18% to $94.1M, primarily driven by the London office lease ($6.2M), headcount additions in compliance (+12 FTEs), and technology infrastructure upgrades. EBITDA margin contracted from 34% to 31%, still within the board-approved 28–35% corridor.

subsections.title: Private Credit
subsections.content: The private credit team deployed $620M in Q1–Q2, well ahead of the $480M plan. Default rates remain at 0.4%, below the 1.2% peer median. Three new institutional LPs were onboarded, contributing $310M in commitments.

subsections.title: Advisory Services
subsections.content: Advisory revenue of $41.6M was 8% below the H1 plan, reflecting deal slippage from three M&A mandates that pushed to H2. Pipeline coverage stands at 2.4× for the remainder of the year, providing confidence in a full-year recovery.

sections.title: Risk & Compliance
bullet_points: No material regulatory findings in the SEC examination completed April 2026
Credit VaR across all funds held within board limits throughout H1
Cybersecurity posture upgraded — SOC 2 Type II audit underway, expected completion August 2026
Concentration risk in two portfolio companies flagged; remediation plan approved by Risk Committee

sections.title: Strategic Priorities for H2
numbered_list: Close Fund IV at $1.8B hard cap by October 2026
Launch Singapore entity to access APAC LP base directly
Implement new portfolio monitoring platform (vendor selected: Allvue)
Complete London team build-out — 4 remaining hires in credit research
Review and renegotiate prime brokerage terms with Goldman and JPMorgan

conclusion: Meridian Capital Partners is on track for its strongest year since founding. The AUM milestone reached ahead of schedule validates the strategic pivot toward private credit and direct lending. Execution on H2 priorities — particularly Fund IV close and the Singapore launch — will determine whether we achieve the upper end of our 2026 guidance. The board's confidence is reflected in the approved $15M budget increase for the London and APAC build-outs.
